newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia crudes weaken as futures slide, Oman weak.
newsitem.headline: Asia crudes weaken as futures slide, Oman weak.

text.p: Asian crude prices were weaker on Monday as tensions in the Gulf eased after Iraq said it would no longer fire at patrolling allied warplanes over the no-fly zone.

Brent futures slumped in late afternoon dealings on Monday as players took profits on the long positions built up during the recent rally. November was down 75 cents in London at $22.38 compared with Friday.
The Brent/Dubai spread on key-month November was quoted earlier in Singapore at $2.25/$2.35, but traders said the slump on Brent futures would narrow the spread.
Dubai intermonth spreads were steady around 40 cents per barrel with November/December at 37/44, December/January at 35/43, while January/February was narrower at 35/40.
Tapis paper for October was offered late Monday at $22.30 with a notional bid at $22.00, while NOvember was offered at $21.90 with a notional bid put at $21.60, down 50 to 60 cents from Friday.
China was looking to replace lost production of 260,000 barrles per day from its Liuhua, Nanhai and Xijiang offshore fields. The fields have been down since last week owing to bad weather.

China was a strong buyer of Minas to make up for the loss of production at the three fields, traders said. They said China bought 600,000 barrels of October Minas at ICP flat to plus five cents. A further 300,000 barrels may have been sold by a Japanes trader to a European major.
A producer asked plus $1.30 for October Tapis and a major was asking Tapis quotes less 10 cents for a late October Kutubu. A major sold Kutubu at Tapis less 30 cents to another major.
